nuggets.title: NTP Step Backward Generates Duplicate Snowflake IDs

scenario.symptoms: Primary key collisions spike on orders table after VM clock correction. Two ID generator nodes emit identical 64-bit IDs milliseconds apart.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Snowflake-style generator uses local wall clock without waiting until caught up after backward step; sequence bits reset while timestamp unchanged.

incident.headline: Clock rollback without guard logic regenerates previously issued timestamp sequences

agenda.goal: Detect backward clock steps, refuse to generate until safe, or use logical clock with lease on time source.
agenda.opener: After NTP corrected the clock backward, we saw duplicate snowflake IDs. How does your generator handle clock skew?

evidence.strong: Monotonic logical clock, sleep until last timestamp if clock moves back, monitor clock drift, prefer synchronized time with bounded error, alert on refusal.
evidence.adequate: Use NTP but no rollback handling.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes wall clock always moves forward.
misconceptions.challenge: What does snowflake do if time goes backward 200ms?

probes: When should the generator stop issuing IDs?
How are sequence bits managed per millisecond?
hints: Wait until clock catches up to last issued ms.
Log and block rather than collide.
agenda.referenceFix: On clock regression, stall generation until time >= last_timestamp; metrics on clock issues.

nuggets.title: Duplicate Worker IDs Collide After Auto-Scale

scenario.symptoms: Collision rate jumps when Kubernetes HPA doubles ID generator pods. Two pods assigned worker_id=17 via modulo on pod name hash clash.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Worker id allocated locally from hash(pod_name) % 1024 without coordination; scale-up creates birthday collisions.

incident.headline: Uncoordinated worker id assignment duplicates machine bits in snowflake layout

agenda.goal: Assign unique worker ids via coordinated lease service or centralized allocator with conflict detection.
agenda.opener: Scaling ID generators caused duplicate worker bits and colliding IDs. How does each node get a unique worker id?

evidence.strong: Lease worker ids from etcd/DB with TTL and renewal, detect conflicts at startup, expand bit width or use UUID for low scale.
evidence.adequate: Manual static worker id config per host.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes hash of pod name is unique across fleet.
misconceptions.challenge: With 1024 slots and 200 pods, what does birthday paradox tell you?

probes: What happens to worker id when pod restarts?
How many bits do you reserve for worker id?
agenda.referenceFix: Central lease of worker ids with heartbeat; refuse start if id taken.

nuggets.title: Sequence Bit Overflow Stalls Generator at Peak QPS

scenario.symptoms: ID API latency spikes to 2s during flash sale while QPS is 80k per node. Generator busy-waits for next millisecond after exhausting 12-bit sequence in one ms.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Single-threaded ID generation per node; no batch preallocation or extra sequence bits; all clients sync-call HTTP API.

incident.headline: Per-millisecond sequence exhaustion throttles ID throughput below business peak

agenda.goal: Meet peak ID rates by scaling nodes, batch allocation, widening sequence bits, or segmenting namespaces.
agenda.opener: At 80k IDs/sec our generator started stalling waiting for the next millisecond. How do you hit required throughput?

evidence.strong: Horizontal scale of generators with unique worker ids, batch prefetch of ids client-side, tune bits for peak ms rate, optional separate numeric spaces per service.
evidence.adequate: Add nodes without throughput math on sequence bits.

misconceptions.pattern: Uses synchronous HTTP per ID at extreme QPS.
misconceptions.challenge: What is max IDs/ms with 12 sequence bits?

probes: How many IDs can one node emit per millisecond?
hints: 4096 ids/ms per node is the ceiling with 12 bits.
agenda.referenceFix: Batch ID allocation API, enough generator nodes for peak, client-side id buffer.

nuggets.title: Client Parses ID Layout That Changed Server Side

scenario.symptoms: Sharding router sends 30% of traffic to wrong database after server adds datacenter bits to ID format. Mobile apps embed timestamp extraction logic.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Clients decode snowflake bitfields assuming old schema; server v2 adds 2 datacenter bits shrinking worker field without version flag.

incident.headline: Undocumented ID bit layout change breaks client-side routing assumptions

agenda.goal: Treat IDs as opaque or version the bit layout with compatibility policy documented to clients.
agenda.opener: Changing our snowflake layout broke mobile shard routing. What is in the 64-bit ID and who is allowed to decode it?

evidence.strong: Opaque ids for clients, server-side mapping for shard, version nibble in id if decoding needed, migration window with dual routing, documented layout semver.
evidence.adequate: Document layout but clients still hardcode.

misconceptions.pattern: Encourages all clients to parse snowflake bitfields.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens when you need another bit for region?

probes: Should mobile apps know shard from id?
How do you migrate layout safely?
agenda.referenceFix: Stop client bit parsing; lookup shard by registry; if parsing required embed version bits.

nuggets.title: Client Retry After Timeout Creates Duplicate Business Records

scenario.symptoms: Users double-charged when checkout retried ID fetch after 504 timeout though server actually allocated ID. Two orders share different IDs for one cart.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Checkout requests new ID per attempt without idempotency key; ID service has no dedupe of client request token.

incident.headline: Non-idempotent ID allocation on client retry creates duplicate orders for one checkout

agenda.goal: Integrate ID generation with client idempotency keys so retries return same id without double side effects.
agenda.opener: A timeout retry got a second order id and we double-charged. How should clients call the ID service safely?

evidence.strong: Client supplies idempotency-key per checkout session, ID service stores key->id mapping 24h, checkout uses business idempotency before payment, return same id on retry.
evidence.adequate: Client generates UUID locally without server dedupe.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes every retry must fetch a brand new id.
misconceptions.challenge: If first request succeeded but response lost, what id should retry use?

probes: How long does ID service remember keys?
hints: Same key should yield same id.
agenda.referenceFix: Idempotent ID API keyed by checkout session; client reuses id on uncertain failures.
